site: Head office, 3 clinical sites and hosted data centre

framework.framework_name: Healthcare IT & Information Security Audit Programme
framework.scope_statement: Audit of information technology general controls (ITGC) and information security controls supporting the delivery and administration of clinical care, including systems processing special category health data.
primary_frameworks: NHS Data Security and Protection Toolkit (DSPT)
HIPAA Security Rule 45 CFR 164 (cross-reference for US-linked entities)

sections.title: Information Security Governance & Policy
sections.objective: Determine whether security is governed by an accountable structure with approved, current and communicated policy.

checks.title: Board-level accountability for data security
checks.control_objective: A named executive (SIRO or equivalent) holds documented accountability for information risk and reports to the board at least quarterly.
checks.test_procedure: Inspect the governance ToR, role description and the last four sets of board/IG committee minutes for evidence of information risk reporting.
evidence_expected: SIRO appointment letter or role profile

checks.title: Information security policy suite approved and current
checks.control_objective: A documented ISMS policy set exists, is approved by management, and is reviewed at least annually or on significant change.
checks.test_procedure: Inspect the policy register. Verify version, approver and review date for a sample of 5 policies. Confirm none are past their review date.
evidence_expected: Sample of 5 approved policies with version control

checks.title: Policy communication and staff acknowledgement
checks.control_objective: Staff and contractors formally acknowledge acceptable use and security policy on onboarding and annually thereafter.
checks.test_procedure: Select 15 staff across clinical, admin and third-party roles. Confirm signed/logged acknowledgement within the last 12 months.

checks.title: Asset inventory completeness
checks.control_objective: A maintained inventory records all information assets and systems processing patient data, with named owners and criticality ratings.
checks.test_procedure: Reconcile the asset register against network discovery output and the finance fixed-asset list. Investigate variances greater than 5%.

sections.title: Risk Management & Compliance Assurance
sections.objective: Assess whether information risk is identified, assessed, treated and monitored on a defined cycle.

checks.title: Information risk register maintained
checks.control_objective: Risks are recorded with inherent/residual scoring, treatment plans, owners and review dates, and are reviewed at least quarterly.
checks.test_procedure: Inspect the risk register. Test 8 risks for completeness of scoring, owner, treatment and evidence of review within 90 days.

checks.title: DPIAs completed for high-risk processing
checks.control_objective: A DPIA is completed and signed off before deployment of any system processing special category health data at scale.
checks.test_procedure: Identify systems introduced in the audit period. For each, confirm a DPIA exists, was completed pre-go-live and was reviewed by the DPO.

checks.title: Independent security testing performed
checks.control_objective: Penetration testing of external-facing and clinical systems is performed at least annually by a competent independent party, with findings tracked to closure.
checks.test_procedure: Inspect the most recent penetration test report. Trace all critical and high findings to the remediation tracker and verify closure evidence.

checks.title: Certification and regulatory submissions current
checks.control_objective: DSPT submission, Cyber Essentials certification and ICO registration are current and not subject to unresolved conditions.
checks.test_procedure: Verify DSPT status against the published portal, inspect the Cyber Essentials certificate expiry, and confirm ICO registration renewal.

sections.title: Identity & Access Management
sections.objective: Verify that access to clinical and administrative systems is granted on least privilege and removed promptly.

checks.title: Joiners, movers, leavers process effectiveness
checks.control_objective: Access is provisioned on documented authorisation and revoked within one working day of termination.
checks.test_procedure: Sample 20 leavers from HR records in the period. Confirm account disablement date in AD/EHR against termination date. Sample 15 joiners for approval evidence.

checks.title: Privileged account governance
checks.control_objective: Administrative accounts are individually assigned, separate from standard accounts, MFA-protected and reviewed quarterly.
checks.test_procedure: Export all members of privileged groups. Test each for named ownership, MFA enrolment, and business justification. Confirm evidence of the last quarterly review.

checks.title: Multi-factor authentication coverage
checks.control_objective: MFA is enforced for all remote access, cloud administrative consoles and email.
checks.test_procedure: Inspect conditional access / MFA policy configuration. Identify and test the exception list for documented approval and compensating controls.

checks.title: Periodic user access recertification
checks.control_objective: System owners recertify user access to clinical systems at least every six months, with removals actioned and evidenced.
checks.test_procedure: Obtain the last recertification for the EHR/PAS. Verify completeness of population, sign-off by the system owner, and that flagged removals were actioned.

checks.title: Shared and generic account control
checks.control_objective: Shared accounts are prohibited, or where clinically unavoidable, are registered, justified, and attributable via compensating controls.
checks.test_procedure: Query directory and EHR for generic account naming patterns. For each identified, confirm registration, approval and attribution mechanism.

sections.title: Data Protection & Privacy
sections.objective: Confirm that processing of special category health data meets UK GDPR obligations.

checks.title: Record of Processing Activities (ROPA) accuracy
checks.control_objective: A ROPA is maintained under Art. 30 covering all processing of health data, with lawful basis and Art. 9 condition documented.
checks.test_procedure: Sample 6 processing activities from the ROPA and trace to the underlying system. Identify any system in the asset register absent from the ROPA.

checks.title: Data retention and secure disposal
checks.control_objective: Retention is applied per the Records Management Code of Practice, with evidenced destruction of records beyond retention.
checks.test_procedure: Inspect the retention schedule. Query a clinical system for records exceeding retention. Inspect destruction certificates for the last disposal cycle.

checks.title: Data subject rights fulfilment within statutory timescales
checks.control_objective: SARs and other rights requests are logged and completed within one calendar month (or a documented extension).
checks.test_procedure: Select 10 requests from the SAR log. Calculate elapsed days from receipt to response. Test for evidence of identity verification and redaction review.

checks.title: International transfers safeguarded
checks.control_objective: Any transfer of personal data outside the UK is supported by adequacy, an IDTA/Addendum, and a transfer risk assessment.
checks.test_procedure: Identify cloud services hosting or supporting patient data. For each non-UK location, inspect the transfer mechanism and TRA.

sections.title: Network & Infrastructure Security
sections.objective: Evaluate perimeter, segmentation and secure configuration controls.

checks.title: Firewall rule base governance
checks.control_objective: Firewall rules are documented, business-justified, reviewed at least every six months, and free of any-any permits.
checks.test_procedure: Export the rule base. Test for any-any rules, rules without justification, and rules unused for 90 days. Inspect the last review sign-off.
evidence_expected: Change tickets for a sample of 5 rules

checks.title: Network segmentation of clinical and medical device VLANs
checks.control_objective: Medical devices, clinical systems, guest Wi-Fi and corporate IT are segmented with enforced inter-VLAN access control.
checks.test_procedure: Inspect the network diagram and VLAN/ACL configuration. Perform connectivity testing from the guest and corporate segments toward the medical device VLAN.

checks.title: Remote access security
checks.control_objective: Remote access is via managed VPN or ZTNA with MFA, device posture checking and session logging. No direct RDP is exposed to the internet.
checks.test_procedure: Review the external attack surface (port scan / ASM output) for exposed management protocols. Inspect VPN configuration and authentication policy.

checks.title: Encryption of data in transit
checks.control_objective: All transmission of patient data uses TLS 1.2 or higher; legacy protocols are disabled.
checks.test_procedure: Run a TLS configuration scan against internal and external endpoints handling patient data. Confirm SSLv3/TLS 1.0/1.1 and weak ciphers are disabled.

sections.title: Endpoint, Mobile & Connected Medical Device Security
sections.objective: Assess controls over devices holding or accessing patient data, including IoMT.

checks.title: Full-disk encryption on all endpoints
checks.control_objective: All laptops, desktops and removable media holding patient data are encrypted to an approved standard.
checks.test_procedure: Extract the encryption compliance report from the endpoint management platform. Reconcile the device count to the asset register and investigate non-compliant devices.

checks.title: Endpoint detection and response coverage
checks.control_objective: EDR/anti-malware is deployed to 100% of in-scope endpoints and servers, with current signatures and alerting to a monitored queue.
checks.test_procedure: Compare EDR console inventory to the asset register. Identify gaps and stale agents (no check-in over 14 days).

checks.title: Mobile device management for clinical mobile use
checks.control_objective: Devices accessing clinical email or apps are enrolled in MDM with enforced passcode, encryption and remote wipe.
checks.test_procedure: Inspect MDM policy configuration. Test conditional access to confirm unmanaged devices are blocked. Sample 10 enrolled devices for policy compliance.

checks.title: Connected medical device (IoMT) risk control
checks.control_objective: Networked medical devices are inventoried, risk-assessed, patched per manufacturer guidance, and covered by a supplier support agreement.
checks.test_procedure: Obtain the medical device inventory. Sample 8 networked devices and test for: OS support status, default credential change, network placement, and manufacturer patch position.

checks.title: Removable media control
checks.control_objective: Use of removable media is blocked by default or restricted to encrypted, approved devices with logging.
checks.test_procedure: Inspect device control policy. Attempt to write to an unencrypted USB device on a sample endpoint. Review removable media usage logs.

sections.title: Vulnerability & Patch Management
sections.objective: Determine whether technical vulnerabilities are identified and remediated within defined timescales.

checks.title: Authenticated vulnerability scanning cadence
checks.control_objective: Credentialed vulnerability scans run at least monthly across all in-scope estate, with results triaged to owners.
checks.test_procedure: Inspect the last three scan cycles. Confirm scan authentication succeeded and that scope covers the full asset register.

checks.title: Patch deployment within defined SLA
checks.control_objective: Critical and high-severity patches are deployed within 14 days of vendor release (Cyber Essentials requires 14 days for critical).
checks.test_procedure: Select 20 critical/high vulnerabilities from the scan data. Calculate days from vendor release to remediation. Report SLA breach rate.

checks.title: Unsupported / end-of-life systems
checks.control_objective: No unsupported operating system or application processes patient data without an extended support agreement and documented compensating controls.
checks.test_procedure: Query the asset register and scan data for EOL platforms. For each, inspect the risk acceptance, expiry date and compensating controls.

checks.title: Secure baseline configuration
checks.control_objective: Hardened build standards exist for servers, endpoints and network devices and are enforced and monitored for drift.
checks.test_procedure: Inspect build standards. Run a configuration compliance scan (e.g. CIS benchmark) against a sample of 5 servers and report the compliance percentage.

sections.title: Change & Development Management
sections.objective: Assess whether changes to clinical systems are authorised, tested and segregated from production.

checks.title: Change authorisation and clinical safety sign-off
checks.control_objective: All production changes are approved via CAB, and changes affecting clinical systems carry DCB0160 clinical safety officer sign-off.
checks.test_procedure: Sample 15 changes from the period. Test for approval prior to implementation, test evidence, back-out plan and clinical safety sign-off where applicable.

checks.title: Segregation of development, test and production
checks.control_objective: Environments are separated, and developers do not hold standing production access.
checks.test_procedure: Inspect environment architecture. Cross-reference the developer group membership against production access groups for conflicts.

checks.title: Use of live patient data in non-production
checks.control_objective: Live patient data is not used for testing unless anonymised/pseudonymised under an approved, documented process.
checks.test_procedure: Query non-production databases for identifiable patient fields. Inspect the data masking process and any approvals for live data use.

checks.title: Emergency change control
checks.control_objective: Emergency changes are retrospectively reviewed and approved within five working days.
checks.test_procedure: Identify all emergency changes in the period. Test for retrospective approval and review of appropriateness.

sections.title: Logging, Monitoring & Detection
sections.objective: Verify that security-relevant events are captured, retained and monitored, including clinical record access.

checks.title: Centralised log collection and retention
checks.control_objective: Security logs from critical systems are forwarded to a central SIEM, protected from alteration and retained for at least six months.
checks.test_procedure: Compare the SIEM log source list to the critical asset list. Verify retention configuration and test log immutability controls.

checks.title: Clinical record access auditing
checks.control_objective: Access to patient records is logged at record level and proactively audited for inappropriate access (e.g. self, family, VIP lookups).
checks.test_procedure: Inspect the EHR audit log configuration. Obtain evidence of proactive audits performed in the period and outcomes of any alerts raised.

checks.title: Alert triage and response coverage
checks.control_objective: Security alerts are triaged within defined timescales by a resourced function (internal or MSSP) with out-of-hours coverage.
checks.test_procedure: Sample 10 alerts. Measure time from generation to triage and closure. Inspect the MSSP contract for coverage hours and SLA.

checks.title: Time synchronisation
checks.control_objective: All systems synchronise to a common authoritative time source to preserve log integrity and forensic admissibility.
checks.test_procedure: Sample 8 systems and compare configured NTP source and current clock drift.

sections.title: Backup, Resilience & Disaster Recovery
sections.objective: Confirm that clinical services can be restored within agreed objectives following disruption or ransomware.

checks.title: Backup coverage and immutability
checks.control_objective: Backups follow 3-2-1 principles with at least one immutable or offline copy that cannot be deleted by a compromised administrator.
checks.test_procedure: Inspect backup job configuration and scope against critical systems. Verify immutability/air-gap settings and that backup admin credentials are separate from domain admin.

checks.title: Restore testing performed and evidenced
checks.control_objective: Full restore tests of critical clinical systems are performed at least annually and meet the defined RTO/RPO.
checks.test_procedure: Inspect the most recent restore test report. Compare actual restore time against documented RTO. Confirm data integrity validation was performed.

checks.title: Business continuity plan for IT outage
checks.control_objective: Documented clinical business continuity procedures exist for extended IT unavailability, including paper fallback, and are exercised annually.
checks.test_procedure: Inspect the BCP and the record of the last exercise. Interview two clinical leads on awareness of downtime procedures.

checks.title: Single points of failure identified
checks.control_objective: Resilience of critical infrastructure (power, connectivity, virtualisation, key personnel) is assessed with mitigation in place.
checks.test_procedure: Inspect the resilience assessment and BIA. Verify UPS/generator test records and dual connectivity arrangements.

sections.title: Third Party & Supplier Assurance
sections.objective: Assess governance over suppliers processing or accessing patient data.

checks.title: Data processing agreements in place
checks.control_objective: Every processor handling patient data is bound by an Art. 28 compliant contract including security, sub-processor and breach notification terms.
checks.test_procedure: Select 10 suppliers from the supplier register handling patient data. Inspect contracts for Art. 28(3) clauses.

checks.title: Supplier security due diligence and ongoing monitoring
checks.control_objective: Suppliers are risk-tiered, assessed before onboarding, and reassessed periodically (e.g. via ISO 27001 certificate, SOC 2 report or DSPT status).
checks.test_procedure: For the same 10 suppliers, inspect onboarding assessments and current assurance artefacts. Check expiry dates of certifications.

checks.title: Third-party remote access control
checks.control_objective: Supplier remote access is time-bound, individually attributed, MFA-protected, approved per session and fully logged.
checks.test_procedure: Identify all third-party accounts in the directory. Test for MFA, expiry dates and last logon. Sample 5 support sessions for approval and session recording.

checks.title: Exit and data return / deletion provisions
checks.control_objective: Contracts specify data return and secure deletion on termination, and deletion certificates are obtained for terminated suppliers.
checks.test_procedure: Identify suppliers terminated in the period. Inspect evidence of data return and certificates of secure deletion.

sections.title: Incident Response & Breach Notification
sections.objective: Determine whether security incidents are detected, managed and reported within regulatory timescales.

checks.title: Incident response plan tested
checks.control_objective: A documented IR plan defines roles, severity criteria and escalation, and is exercised at least annually including a ransomware scenario.
checks.test_procedure: Inspect the IR plan and the most recent tabletop exercise report. Verify actions from lessons learned were closed.

checks.title: Breach notification within 72 hours
checks.control_objective: Notifiable personal data breaches are reported to the ICO within 72 hours and, where required, to data subjects without undue delay.
checks.test_procedure: Review all incidents classified as personal data breaches. Calculate elapsed time from awareness to ICO/DSPT toolkit reporting.

checks.title: Incident logging and root cause analysis
checks.control_objective: All security incidents are logged centrally with categorisation, root cause and corrective actions tracked to closure.
checks.test_procedure: Sample 10 incidents. Test for completeness of record, RCA where severity warrants, and closure of corrective actions.

checks.title: Forensic readiness and evidence handling
checks.control_objective: Procedures exist for evidence preservation, and retained logs are sufficient to support investigation.
checks.test_procedure: Inspect forensic readiness procedures. Confirm log retention supports the detection dwell-time assumption stated in the risk assessment.

sections.title: Physical & Environmental Security
sections.objective: Assess physical protection of infrastructure and areas where patient data is visible or stored.

checks.title: Data centre / comms room access control
checks.control_objective: Access to server and comms rooms is restricted to authorised personnel, logged, and reviewed at least six-monthly.
checks.test_procedure: Obtain the access control list for the comms room. Test each holder for continued business need. Inspect the access log for unexplained entries.

checks.title: Clear screen and unattended workstation controls
checks.control_objective: Automatic screen lock is enforced, and workstations in patient-facing areas are positioned to prevent unauthorised viewing.
checks.test_procedure: Inspect the GPO screen-lock timeout. Walk reception and clinical areas at two points during the day and record observations of unattended unlocked screens.

checks.title: Secure disposal of IT assets
checks.control_objective: IT assets are sanitised to an approved standard before disposal or reuse, with certificates retained and asset records updated.
checks.test_procedure: Select 10 assets disposed of in the period. Trace to destruction certificates and confirm removal from the asset register.

checks.title: Environmental controls in technical areas
checks.control_objective: Comms rooms have appropriate cooling, fire suppression and water/temperature alerting, and are not used for general storage.
checks.test_procedure: Physically inspect technical areas. Review environmental monitoring alerts and maintenance records for the period.

sections.title: People, Training & Security Culture
sections.objective: Evaluate whether staff are screened, trained and tested against social engineering.

checks.title: Annual data security training completion
checks.control_objective: At least 95% of staff, including contractors and board members, complete annual data security awareness training.
checks.test_procedure: Obtain the LMS completion report. Calculate the completion rate against the current headcount. Test that non-completers have been escalated.

checks.title: Pre-employment screening
checks.control_objective: Identity, right to work, references and DBS (where applicable) are verified before access to patient data is granted.
checks.test_procedure: Sample 12 personnel files for staff who joined in the period and test for completed screening prior to their system access start date.

checks.title: Phishing simulation programme
checks.control_objective: Simulated phishing exercises are run at least quarterly with targeted follow-up training for repeat click-throughs.
checks.test_procedure: Review simulation results for the last four quarters. Analyse the click and report rate trend and confirm remedial training was assigned.

checks.title: Confidentiality obligations and disciplinary process
checks.control_objective: Contracts include confidentiality clauses that survive termination, and a disciplinary process is applied for confidentiality breaches.
checks.test_procedure: Inspect the standard contract template and the disciplinary policy. Review any confidentiality breach cases in the period for consistent handling.

scope_notes: Fieldwork covered central IT infrastructure, the electronic health record, PACS, the practice management system and supporting cloud services. Clinical practice, medical device efficacy and financial controls were outside scope. Forensic readiness testing (IRM-04) was deferred at management request and will be covered in the next cycle; this constitutes a scope limitation.
notice: WORKED EXAMPLE — NOT A REAL AUDIT. Northgate Health Group is a fictional organisation and every finding below is illustrative. This report was generated by the open-source healthcare IT audit tool at github.com/ajaytony1411-ajse/healthcare-it-audit-tool--10 to demonstrate its output. It contains no real patient data and describes no real organisation's security posture.

ISG-01.observation: Control tested and found to be operating effectively; no exceptions identified in the sample.

ISG-02.observation: Control tested and found to be operating effectively; no exceptions identified in the sample.

ISG-03.observation: Control tested and found to be operating effectively; no exceptions identified in the sample.

ISG-04.observation: The asset register records 612 hosts against 671 identified by network discovery, a variance of 8.8%. 43 entries have no named owner and criticality ratings are absent for all non-server assets.
ISG-04.root_cause: The register is maintained manually in a spreadsheet and updated only at procurement, not at decommission or discovery.
ISG-04.risk_statement: Assets outside the register are outside patching, monitoring and backup scope, and cannot be protected or recovered.
ISG-04.corrective_action: Move the register to the endpoint management platform as the source of truth, with monthly automated reconciliation against discovery and exception reporting.

RSK-01.observation: Control tested and found to be operating effectively; no exceptions identified in the sample.

RSK-02.observation: Four new systems processing patient data were deployed in the period. DPIAs exist for three; the patient messaging platform went live without one and the DPIA was completed retrospectively 5 months after go-live. Two DPIAs lack evidence of DPO review.
RSK-02.root_cause: The DPIA trigger sits in the IG process but is not a mandatory gate in the project or procurement lifecycle, so it can be bypassed.
RSK-02.risk_statement: Deploying high-risk processing without a prior DPIA is a direct breach of UK GDPR Art. 35 and removes the opportunity to design in mitigations before go-live.
RSK-02.corrective_action: Make DPIA completion and DPO sign-off a mandatory stage gate in the project and procurement lifecycle, with the CAB unable to approve go-live without it.

RSK-03.observation: Control tested and found to be operating effectively; no exceptions identified in the sample.

RSK-04.observation: The organisation is an independent provider and is not required to submit the DSPT; the equivalent assurance is provided through ISO 27001 certification, which was verified as current. Cyber Essentials Plus and ICO registration were confirmed in date.

IAM-01.observation: 20 leavers were sampled against HR termination records. 7 accounts (35%) remained enabled after the leave date, the longest for 94 days. Two of these accounts were used to authenticate to the EHR after the individual had left the organisation.
IAM-01.root_cause: Leaver notification is a manual email from HR to the service desk with no ticket raised, no SLA and no reconciliation between HR records and Active Directory.
IAM-01.risk_statement: Active credentials held by former staff allow unauthorised access to special category health data. Post-termination logons already evidenced constitute a reportable personal data breach exposure under UK GDPR Art. 33.
IAM-01.corrective_action: Automate leaver de-provisioning from the HR system to Active Directory. As an interim control, implement a monthly reconciliation of the HR leaver report against enabled accounts, with exceptions reported to the IG committee. Investigate the two post-termination logons as potential incidents.
IAM-01.action_owner: Head of IT Operations / HR Director

IAM-02.observation: 31 accounts hold Domain Admin or equivalent privilege. 9 are shared or service accounts without a named owner, and 4 have not been used in over 180 days. Quarterly privileged access reviews were evidenced for Q1 and Q2 only; Q3 and Q4 were not performed.
IAM-02.root_cause: No privileged access management tooling; reviews depend on the availability of a single infrastructure engineer with no deputy.
IAM-02.risk_statement: Excessive and unattributable administrative access increases the blast radius of a compromised credential and prevents attribution during investigation.
IAM-02.corrective_action: Reduce privileged accounts to named individuals with a documented justification, disable dormant accounts, and place remaining service accounts under managed vault credentials. Reinstate quarterly review with a named deputy reviewer.

IAM-03.observation: Control tested and found to be operating effectively; no exceptions identified in the sample.

IAM-04.observation: Control tested and found to be operating effectively; no exceptions identified in the sample.

IAM-05.observation: Control tested and found to be operating effectively; no exceptions identified in the sample.

DPR-01.observation: Control tested and found to be operating effectively; no exceptions identified in the sample.

DPR-02.observation: Control tested and found to be operating effectively; no exceptions identified in the sample.

DPR-03.observation: Of 10 subject access requests sampled, 8 were completed within one calendar month, 1 took 47 days with no extension notified, and 1 remained open at 62 days. Identity verification was evidenced in all cases.
DPR-03.root_cause: SAR handling rests with a single IG officer with no cover during absence, and no escalation triggers when a request approaches 21 days.
DPR-03.risk_statement: Late responses without a notified extension breach UK GDPR Art. 12(3) and are a common trigger for ICO complaints.
DPR-03.corrective_action: Introduce automated escalation at day 21, cross-train a second officer, and report open SAR aging to the IG committee monthly.

DPR-04.observation: Control tested and found to be operating effectively; no exceptions identified in the sample.

NET-01.observation: Control tested and found to be operating effectively; no exceptions identified in the sample.

NET-02.observation: Medical device and corporate VLANs are separated, but ACL testing from the corporate segment reached 4 of 8 medical devices tested on management ports (SSH/HTTP). Guest Wi-Fi was correctly isolated. The network diagram was last updated 14 months ago and did not reflect two new VLANs.
NET-02.root_cause: Segmentation was implemented at project level without an enforced inter-VLAN policy baseline, and no periodic validation testing takes place.
NET-02.risk_statement: Lateral movement from a compromised corporate endpoint to connected medical devices could affect device availability and, in some device classes, patient safety.
NET-02.corrective_action: Apply default-deny inter-VLAN policy with explicit allow rules for clinically required flows. Re-test segmentation after change and at least annually. Refresh the network diagram and place it under change control.

NET-03.observation: Control tested and found to be operating effectively; no exceptions identified in the sample.

NET-04.observation: Control tested and found to be operating effectively; no exceptions identified in the sample.

END-01.observation: Control tested and found to be operating effectively; no exceptions identified in the sample.

END-02.observation: Control tested and found to be operating effectively; no exceptions identified in the sample.

END-03.observation: Control tested and found to be operating effectively; no exceptions identified in the sample.

END-04.observation: The medical device inventory holds 218 networked devices but is not reconciled to network discovery, which identified 27 further devices. Of 8 devices sampled, 3 ran unsupported operating systems and 2 retained default administrative credentials.
END-04.root_cause: Medical devices are procured by clinical departments without IT involvement, so they do not enter the IT asset or vulnerability management processes.
END-04.risk_statement: Unmanaged connected devices with default credentials provide a persistent foothold on the clinical network and, for some device classes, present a patient safety risk.
END-04.corrective_action: Include IT security sign-off as a mandatory step in medical device procurement. Reconcile the inventory to discovery quarterly. Change default credentials on the devices identified and obtain manufacturer patch positions for unsupported devices.
END-04.action_owner: Head of Medical Physics / IT Security Manager

END-05.observation: Control tested and found to be operating effectively; no exceptions identified in the sample.

VUL-01.observation: Control tested and found to be operating effectively; no exceptions identified in the sample.

VUL-02.observation: Of 20 critical and high vulnerabilities sampled, 13 exceeded the 14-day remediation SLA. Mean time to remediate for critical vulnerabilities was 47 days. Three internet-facing systems carried unpatched vulnerabilities with known public exploits at the time of testing.
VUL-02.root_cause: Patching windows for clinical systems require clinical sign-off that is only sought monthly, and there is no emergency patching route for actively exploited vulnerabilities.
VUL-02.risk_statement: Exploitation of known vulnerabilities on internet-facing infrastructure is the most common initial access vector in healthcare ransomware incidents. Failure also breaches Cyber Essentials certification conditions.
VUL-02.corrective_action: Define and approve an emergency patching procedure for actively exploited vulnerabilities with a 72-hour target. Remediate the three internet-facing systems immediately. Report SLA compliance monthly to the IG committee.

VUL-03.observation: 14 Windows Server 2012 R2 hosts and 2 Windows 10 21H2 endpoints remain in service, including the radiology PACS gateway. No extended security updates are purchased and no risk acceptance has been formally approved.
VUL-03.root_cause: Replacement of the PACS gateway is dependent on a supplier upgrade that has been deferred twice; no compensating controls were implemented while the deferral ran.
VUL-03.risk_statement: Unsupported platforms receive no security updates and cannot be brought into a defensible position. Compromise of the PACS gateway would disrupt diagnostic imaging and expose patient images.
VUL-03.corrective_action: Produce a dated decommissioning plan for all end-of-life hosts. Where migration cannot complete within 90 days, isolate the hosts to a restricted VLAN with explicit allow rules and obtain formal risk acceptance from the SIRO.

VUL-04.observation: Control tested and found to be operating effectively; no exceptions identified in the sample.

CHG-01.observation: Control tested and found to be operating effectively; no exceptions identified in the sample.

CHG-02.observation: Control tested and found to be operating effectively; no exceptions identified in the sample.

CHG-03.observation: The UAT instance of the EHR contains a full copy of live patient data refreshed monthly, including names, NHS numbers and clinical notes. 34 users have access to UAT, of whom 9 have no clinical role. No masking process exists and no approval for the use of live data was found.
CHG-03.root_cause: The test refresh process was inherited from the previous supplier's implementation and has never been reviewed against data protection requirements.
CHG-03.risk_statement: Patient data is processed in an environment with weaker access control and no clinical justification, contrary to the purpose limitation and security principles. A compromise of UAT would be a reportable breach of the full patient record.
CHG-03.corrective_action: Implement pseudonymisation on refresh to non-production, or restrict UAT access to the same population as production pending that capability. Document and approve the process through the DPO.

CHG-04.observation: Control tested and found to be operating effectively; no exceptions identified in the sample.

LOG-01.observation: Control tested and found to be operating effectively; no exceptions identified in the sample.

LOG-02.observation: The EHR records record-level access, but no proactive audit of inappropriate access has been performed in the audit period. No alerting exists for self-lookup, same-surname or VIP record access. A sample query run during fieldwork identified 3 instances of staff accessing their own record.
LOG-02.root_cause: Ownership of clinical record access auditing is not assigned; IG assumes IT performs it, IT assumes IG performs it.
LOG-02.risk_statement: Inappropriate access to patient records goes undetected. This is a recurring theme in ICO enforcement against healthcare providers and undermines the confidentiality obligation under UK GDPR Art. 5(1)(f).
LOG-02.corrective_action: Assign ownership of clinical audit review to the IG team. Implement monthly proactive audit covering self, same-surname and VIP access, with exceptions investigated under the disciplinary process. Review the 3 instances identified during fieldwork.

LOG-03.observation: Control tested and found to be operating effectively; no exceptions identified in the sample.

LOG-04.observation: Of 8 systems sampled, 2 network appliances synchronise to an external NTP source rather than the internal authoritative source, with observed drift of up to 4 minutes.
LOG-04.root_cause: Appliance builds were not covered by the standard NTP configuration baseline.
LOG-04.risk_statement: Inconsistent timestamps complicate correlation of events across systems during investigation and can undermine evidential reliability.
LOG-04.corrective_action: Add NTP source to the network device build standard and correct the two appliances.

BCP-01.observation: Control tested and found to be operating effectively; no exceptions identified in the sample.

BCP-02.observation: No full restore test of the EHR has been performed since the platform migration 19 months ago. Testing is limited to individual file-level restores. The documented RTO of 4 hours has therefore never been validated.
BCP-02.root_cause: Restore testing requires an isolated recovery environment that has not been funded.
BCP-02.risk_statement: In a ransomware scenario the organisation cannot demonstrate that clinical systems can be recovered within the stated RTO. Unvalidated backups are a recurring cause of extended clinical downtime.
BCP-02.corrective_action: Perform a full restore test of the EHR and PACS to an isolated environment within 60 days, measure actual recovery time against RTO, and repeat at least annually. Report the result to the board.

BCP-03.observation: Control tested and found to be operating effectively; no exceptions identified in the sample.

BCP-04.observation: Control tested and found to be operating effectively; no exceptions identified in the sample.

TPR-01.observation: Of 10 suppliers processing patient data, 8 hold Art. 28 compliant contracts. 2 operate under purchase-order terms only with no data processing clauses, one of which hosts patient-facing appointment data. This finding was raised in the prior year audit and remains open.
TPR-01.root_cause: Contract remediation was assigned to procurement but no completion date was tracked after the original owner left the organisation.
TPR-01.risk_statement: Without Art. 28 terms the organisation cannot demonstrate that processors are bound to appropriate security, sub-processor and breach notification obligations, and remains liable as controller.
TPR-01.corrective_action: Execute data processing agreements with both suppliers or cease the processing. Reassign ownership of the prior-year action and report closure to the audit committee.

TPR-02.observation: Control tested and found to be operating effectively; no exceptions identified in the sample.

TPR-03.observation: 21 third-party support accounts were identified. 6 lack MFA, 11 have no expiry date set, and per-session approval is not required for 4 suppliers who hold standing access. Session logging is in place for all accounts.
TPR-03.root_cause: Supplier access is provisioned ad hoc at contract start with no standard control baseline and no periodic review.
TPR-03.risk_statement: Standing, unattributed supplier access is a well-documented initial access route in healthcare supply chain incidents and limits the ability to attribute activity.
TPR-03.corrective_action: Apply a supplier access standard: MFA mandatory, accounts disabled by default and enabled per approved session, maximum 12-month expiry, quarterly review by the contract owner.

TPR-04.observation: Control tested and found to be operating effectively; no exceptions identified in the sample.

IRM-01.observation: An incident response plan exists and was updated in the period. The last tabletop exercise was 22 months ago and did not cover a ransomware scenario. Four of six lessons learned from that exercise remain open.
IRM-01.root_cause: Exercising is not scheduled in the assurance calendar and competes with operational priorities.
IRM-01.risk_statement: An untested plan and unclosed lessons reduce the effectiveness of response at the point of a real incident, extending clinical downtime.
IRM-01.corrective_action: Run a ransomware tabletop covering clinical downtime and board communications within 90 days, involving clinical leadership. Close the four outstanding actions and schedule exercising annually in the assurance calendar.

IRM-02.observation: Control tested and found to be operating effectively; no exceptions identified in the sample.

IRM-03.observation: Control tested and found to be operating effectively; no exceptions identified in the sample.

PHY-01.observation: The comms room access list holds 23 people, of whom 5 have left the organisation or changed role. The last documented access review was 16 months ago. Access logs are retained but not reviewed.
PHY-01.root_cause: The access list is owned by Facilities and is not linked to the leaver process or the IT access review cycle.
PHY-01.risk_statement: Unauthorised physical access to network infrastructure bypasses logical controls entirely and would not be detected.
PHY-01.corrective_action: Remove the 5 invalid holders immediately. Bring comms room access into the six-monthly access review cycle and the leaver checklist.

PHY-02.observation: Control tested and found to be operating effectively; no exceptions identified in the sample.

AWR-01.observation: Annual data security training completion was 87% against the 95% DSPT threshold. Completion among medical staff was 71% and among board members 60%. Non-completion is not escalated to line managers.
AWR-01.root_cause: Training is assigned via the LMS but completion is not linked to appraisal or to system access, and no escalation route exists.
AWR-01.risk_statement: The organisation does not meet the DSPT training standard, which affects the toolkit submission. Untrained staff are materially more likely to fall to phishing.
AWR-01.corrective_action: Escalate non-completion to line managers at 30 days and to executive leads at 60 days. Link completion to the appraisal process. Report completion rates by staff group monthly to the IG committee.
